citation_title: Sentiment Intensity Ranking among Adjectives Using Sentiment Bearing Word Embeddings
citation_conference_title: Proceedings of the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
og:title: Sentiment Intensity Ranking among Adjectives Using Sentiment Bearing Word Embeddings
og:description: Raksha Sharma, Arpan Somani, Lakshya Kumar, Pushpak Bhattacharyya. Proceedings of the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing. 2017.

abstract: Abstract Identification of intensity ordering among polar (positive or negative) words which have the same semantics can lead to a fine-grained sentiment analysis. For example, ‘master’, ‘seasoned’ and ‘familiar’ point to different intensity levels, though they all convey the same meaning (semantics), i.e., expertise: having a good knowledge of. In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised technique that uses sentiment bearing word embeddings to produce a continuous ranking among adjectives that share common semantics. Our system demonstrates a strong Spearman’s rank correlation of 0.83 with the gold standard ranking. We show that sentiment bearing word embeddings facilitate a more accurate intensity ranking system than other standard word embeddings (word2vec and GloVe). Word2vec is the state-of-the-art for intensity ordering task.
